Question: How safe is it to travel to Varanasi alone since I have never travelled alone earlier?
Answer: Very safe but follow certain precautions! I have been living in Varanasi since 2017 and I do feel qualified to answer this question a an ex-outsider and a current local. (Kal Bhairao Temple) After entering Varanasi, it is a tradition to take blessings from Kal Bhairao. Kal bhairao is believed to be the Kotwal (Police Officer) of Varanasi. I suppose you’re planning to stay for a few days in Varanasi. You can get any guest house at reasonable prices near the Ghats and surrounding areas. They are well maintained and reasonably secure. You can visit our Nepali Dharmashaala as well, if you’re tight on budget. You can DM me on Instagram (Link in bio) (Nepali Mandir and Nepali Dharmashaalaa) What are the precautions? 1.Beware of people offering you intoxicants: Often, it might lead you getting robbed. 2. Don’t take pictures of cremation: Respect Hindu tradition and the family of the deceased. Locals can demand heavy price and might throw away your camera in the river as well. 3. Don’t take bath alone: When you decide to take a dip in Ganga river, make sure the locals are around. What happens is due to increase in water level, the temples and the structures besides the stairs of the Ghat get submerged in the water. Many people , mostly who don’t know swimming and some experienced swimmers have also drowned getting stuck. (Picture source: Pinterest) You see, water levels rises above that as well, and there might be many such structures beneath where there are high chances of getting stuck. 4. Its not city for nightlife: It is advisable not to take a stroll especially around the narrow streets late at night. You might encounter with drunkards, angry cows and bulls. Cows are specially irritated at night when they’re trying to take rest. 5. Be aware of Food choices: Make sure the food is piping hot and served fresh. Be aware if you have leaky gut or any other problems, since the food here consists a lot of masala, a lot of ghee but a lot of love as well. 6. Beware of high prices: If you’re planning to take the boat ride, don’t get surprised to hear ridiculous price. A fair thing to do is to ask the local tea-seller about the prices of the boat ride while enjoying your cup of tea. And, you’ll be asked a ridiculous price for sarees also. I find Golghar sarees to be of best quality and value for money. You can check them out online as well: Buy Designer Ethnic Wear from Banaras | golghar.org They’re just near Kal Bhairao Temple, remember, the Kotwal of the city. So, is Varanasi safe for solo travel? Absolutely yes. You’ll get one of the most amazing experiences of your life. Varanasi is the city of Shiva, The Mahākāla. Mahākāla means beyond time and death, and Varanasi, one of the oldest city of the world, also justifies it fully. Happy travelling. Har Har Mahadev!

Question: Is CA really tough?
Answer: I qualified CA after failing 2 years straight! Let me tell you my story! Normal working hours would be around 16–17 during peak time (4–5 months straight). There are instances where I’d leave home at 6AM, attend my lectures, report to office at 10:30 and then back to home at around 2AM. And with all the unhealthy food from “starred” hotels, and no exercise plus some other unhealthy habits and choices, I got serious health problems, both physical and mental. I was burnt out. Later, I realized, it was due to antibiotics, which I consumed a month before for my skin problems. I managed to pass all the papers except that one and because of that, I had to take Group-I again (There are 2 groups of papers, 4 each.) Failed because of ICAI’s System Okay, come May, 2018 paper. This time I was sure I’d pass. And, here I failed again because of “Auditing” paper. The irony, I worked at an Audit firm for 3 years. Question: Will a smoker’s lungs clean themselves if they quit smoking and how long does it take?
Answer: The latest scientific research says “Yes!” Who conducted the research? The research was carried out by Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute, University College London and Kyoto University in Japan. It was published in Nature journal. The research took genetic samples from 16 people consisting of 3 children, 4 people who never smoked, 3 current smokers and 6 ex smokers (who smoked about a pack of cigarette everyday for about 40 years). What was found in the research? It was found that current smokers had more than 2 times probability of cancer than the people who never smoked. Scientists were surprised that , smokers upon quitting seemed to develop the protective cells which were dormant during smoking to protect itself from the harm of tobacco. The damaged cells due to smoking consisted of 90–96% of total lung cells. Our heroes , the remaining 4–10% remained inactive, protecting themselves from tobacco. Maybe like Shield of Captain America. When people quit smoking, those dormant cells (protective cells) developed , multiplied itself and formed 20–40% of total lung cells. These new generated cells were exactly like the cells of people who never smoked (termed normal lung cells) This can be further explained from the picture below: (Picture Credits: Sanger) In the above picture, White lung cells can be taken as good cells while pink can be taken as damaged ones. From the research it seems like nature is keeping its reserved army which is able to regenerate and multiply itself. How long does it take to recover? It depends on the quantum of damage. 4–5 years can be taken in the safer side. How to go forward with recovery? These best practices can be followed. What are your experiences? Question: What is the most deceiving thing about fitness?
Answer: Our ignorance! This is due to lack of our understanding and experience. Although I am not implying that I know it all, certainly not, however, I am not hesitant to test and improvise which has made me learn a thing or two about fitness. 1.Scales and BMIs are very deceiving: I often hear people saying about Goal Weight etc. Unless, you’re in a competitive sports, don’t run after “Goal Weights”. There is no such thing as perfect BMI. BMIs are very deceiving. It doesn’t take into account the percentage of fat and muscles in our body. One Kilo (2.2 lbs) of fat has way more volume than a kilo of muscle. Most often we are losing on size but get demotivated looking at scale. This is because, we are losing fats and developing muscle. The scale might also show increase in weight, whilst you may be losing on size and improving your health but many a times, people get demotivated. I rarely measure my weight. Remember, weight is just the symptom. (They might have the same weight) 2. It is an ongoing process Many of us think that we would take this 90 day course, follow this diet regimen and then boom, we would become Super Saiyan Goku. This is not how it works. Workout is just like taking a shower or rather brushing your teeth. With time, you will be accustomed to the dopamine and endorphins after the workout, and it becomes a part of your daily life. What if you don’t workout then? The same when you won’t brush your teeth. As simple as that. So, choose what works the best for you and what you can follow for the long term. Choose a workout that you can follow and a diet plan that you can stick to. Dancing, yoga, running, lifting, calisthenics, Floreio, Capoeira , you choose , just move! If you don’t know where to start , you can follow: FREE 30 Day Home Workout For Beginners To Lose Weight Or, Get Your 30 Days Beginner's Yoga Program 3. Its all about mindset One thing that people often fail to understand is that we’re not training our body, rather we’re training our mind instead. Body training is just a by-product , a side effect. There are many Yogis who don’t have ripped physique but, are extremely fit and are capable of doing things we can’t even imagine. I am not discounting the benefit of a ripped body, and sometimes, I too wish I had six packs (and I work for it as well), its good to have it and it is an indicator that a person is inclined towards fitness, but we often take it as a benchmark, which might not be an optimal conclusion to derive (I have seen many people with ripped body including me, suffering from severe aches in body. P.S. It was about an year and half ago; I have chosen a more holistic path to fitness, and on continuous trials and errors, have found what works the best for me, at least for now) These are the three main things that I learnt about fitness. They seemed deceptive, but I realized I was ignorant.

Question: What are the 7 best exercise tips?
Answer: I have been exercising for past 3 years, and there are many tips that I’d like to pass on from my experience. Here’s the best 7 ones: 1.Follow a workout program: Failing to plan is planning to fail. Always follow a particular workout program, designed in such a way that your muscles get taxed in a progressive way. You don’t want to under/over train. And, a workout program will keep you motivated to do complete the predefined tasks and measure your progress as well. Can check out the Free 30 day workout program here: FREE 30 Day Home Workout For Beginners To Lose Weight Or, if you’re into bodyweight and yoga, you can get the free 30 day yoga here: Get Your 30 Days Beginner's Yoga Program 2. Pre workout warm up: Do some dynamic mobility warm-ups before working out. Avoid stretching, just do some mobility training. It warms up your muscles, and reduces the rate of injury. Even Bruce Lee didn’t do warmup before his routine and got a back injury. From the Archives : Bruce Lee's Back Injury You can follow this 5 minute routine: 3. Post workout Stretches: Post workout stretches is very important especially if you’re lifting heavy. It makes easier for the muscles to deal with the injuries. It saves you a lot of injury trouble and with DOMS as well. You can simply follow this 5 minutes stretch. 4. Do not miss out on cardio: Strength and all is okay but if you can’t run, there’s not point in your fitness. Remember to do strength training before cardio. 5. For busy schedule : If you’re short on time, then High Intensity Interval Training is a go to option. Too much work in too less time. It requires you to give your full efforts for a short period of time and then rest for a certain time and again , giving your full efforts. Example: Run as hard as you can for 20 seconds, then for 30 seconds, do simple jogging, then again run hard for 20 seconds and jog for 30 seconds. (You can reduce jog time, as per you fitness level). Do this for about 15–20 minutes. 6. Don’t miss out on breathing exercises/pranayama: I can’t emphasize enough the role of breathing exercises in your workout regimen. It helps in quick recovery, improves your strength, endurance and immunity. One very little example: I could only do 5–6 pull-ups, but after I incorporated pranyama, I could easily do 10 pull-ups. It will defer from person to person. What you can do is: Take 30 deep breaths (During inhalation, your belly and chest should expand and should squeeze during exhalation), and then on the last breath hold it. Hold it as much as you can, typically 1–2 minutes, it depends on your fitness level. Continue it for 2–3 rounds. You can include other pranyama like Kapalbhaati or Anulom Vilom 7. Nutrition/Water and Intermittent Fasting: Have plenty of fresh raw fruits and vegetables. Take ample amount of Fats like ghee, butter, nuts etc. Drink water by checking how your body responds. There is no specific number of liters of water per day one should drink. Make sure the pee is clear and you don’t feel dehydrated. Intermittent fasting is a must for exercise doers, as during the workout, old muscles get damaged and new muscle originates. The dead muscle proteins are not excreted which creates problem in our body like ageing, arthritis etc. During intermittent fasting, the dead proteins get excreted and will help tremendously on your overall health. I have written quite a few answers in this topic. Make sure to check it out. These are the 7 best tips that I personally follow and have reaped tremendous benefits. What do you follow? Name: CA. Suyog Upadhyaya
Question: How can I become fluent in English?
Answer: Here’s some practical & [ (secret ;) ] tips how a non-native English speaker like me became fluent in English : A bit of a background: I was born in Nepal and completed my schooling here. Although I was privileged enough to join an English school since I was a kid, I was very poor in English. In 6th standard I joined a new school and I felt kind of left out. Everyone used to watch English movies, listen to English songs and I couldn’t even understand a single word. Then in the first terminal examination, I got bad grades because of English Grammar. Then I decided, I will not let English take over my self-esteem. So what did I do? 1.Read a lot: I read a lot of English books. I started with very basic fairy tale stories. I used to speak out loud while reading so that I could get hang of the words. Of course I didn’t spell perfectly but it was worth the effort. Gradually moving to simple novels and newspapers. I really enjoyed reading books from the school library. You have the added benefit of reading here in Quora ;) 2. Speak a lot: I sought help from my brother as well, he was small kid back then, he probably doesn’t even remember us making this pact at home that we would speak in English. There were some cool friends as well, with whom I made this pact of speaking in English. Now, there are various Apps where you can connect to strangers and speak in English. You can check out on PlayStore or apple store. Note: Do not think that people will make fun of you! Even if they make its their problem, we are trying to improve, let them see after an year. Be determined! If someone tells you , you have a bad English and asks you to stop, just tell them Suyog forced you to speak, put the BLAME ON ME! but Never Stop! 3. Build your vocabulary : As per Michael Thomas, great linguist and a great language teacher, there are only 1500 words that newspapers use on daily basis. Make a habit of learning new words daily. Keep your notes handy and revisit the words whenever you have free time. 15 words a day and you will be perfect in 100 days (about 3 Months) 4. Watch English Contents: Start with simple cartoons and then gradually advance to Series and Movies. You might want to use subtitles at first and then gradually removing the subtitles off! I still use subtitles sometimes mostly when I watch any content of British accent. That’s just me. 5. Write : Make a journal, write a story , write here on Quora. There are many options available. Just put in the work. 6. Grammar : Grammar is very important, but when we are just starting out, do not focus much on grammar. Just try to move, and put in your work. There are many apps that will teach you English grammar. Main thing is that we should be able to communicate ourselves properly. How long will it take? I do not know, but with 1–2 hours of practice, one should be pretty comfortable with English in 2–3 Months. Anything to keep in mind? Do not ever lose hope. There are good days and there are bad days, we just have to keep our composure and move forward. Just put in your diligent efforts! Wishing you a good life. Regards, Suyog

Question: Is it OK to eat one egg a day?
Answer: I used eat a DOZEN, EVERYDAY!!! Little Background : I come from a traditional vegetarian family from Nepal. I hadn’t had any eggs or any meat since I was a child. 3 years back, I decided to take control over my health and got into exercise and started taking Eggs! I used to take a dozen boiled eggs. What was my initial thought? There are many studies that show that Eggs raise cholesterol, whilst there are other studies that show that eating eggs actually increases Good Cholesterol level. So much confusion. Pheww!! Why did I do that? First of all I did that for about a month. I wanted to check the actual results since there are many theories and researches around. Its better to check for ourselves. (Curious sheep :D ) Most importantly, I was working out as well, and had a very little muscle mass, so I thought it would be a good source of proteins. Also the following points were conisdered: 1. Whole eggs promotes greater stimulation of post exercise muscle protein synthesis *. Simply meaning, eggs help in muscle growth and recovery. 2. Eggs are very high in nutrients. They have practically every vitamin and mineral except vitamin C. 3. Eggs are loaded with healthy fats. They contain omega-3 fatty acids, including DHA and EPA. NEED THAT GAINZ!! ;) So what happened? I got fed up with eggs within a month. It certainly didn’t raise my cholesterol level while my workouts were improving as well. But there are various factors to be taken into consideration. I was taking enough veggies and fruits and I cut on sugar as well. Do I recommend? A Dozen a day? CERTAINLY NOT A couple of eggs a day : If you love it, Certainly, YES ! Why don’t I eat eggs now? I’ve been into meditation for quite a few time now and I don’t feel like eating it. While eggs are very healthy for physical growth, its just that, there was a natural call not to eat it. If in future , I want to eat, I will eat again, but there are various plant based nutrient / protein sources that work really well. In short, you can definitely eat an egg per day, just have to check what works for you! Wishing you a good health and a good life! Regards, Reference: * Stephan van Vliet, Evan L Shy, Sidney Abou Sawan, Joseph W Beals, Daniel WD West, Sarah K Skinner, Alexander V Ulanov, Zhong Li, Scott A Paluska, Carl M Parsons, Daniel R Moore, Nicholas A Burd, Consumption of whole eggs promotes greater stimulation of postexercise muscle protein synthesis than consumption of isonitrogenous amounts of egg whites in young men, The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, Volume 106, Issue 6, December 2017, Pages 1401–1412

Question: What happens if you do not eat sugar for 8 weeks?
Answer: I DID IT FOR 8 MONTHS!!! So what happened? Background: I used to eat chocolates and ice cream frequently. And because of poor eating habits and no exercise, I was a pretty obese guy. I used to suffer from common cold frequently as well. 3 years ago, I decided that I will cut sugar out of my diet. The only point I consider while eating sweet is, “Am I getting addicted to it?” . Sometimes, I get sweet cravings, and that’s the time I decide not to take it, just to develop my will power. Name: CA. Suyog Upadhyaya
Question: What is the deal with the present trend of "intermittent" fasting for weight loss?
Answer: Intermittent Fasting has been the style of eating since the beginning of history (Picture Source: Pixabay) Early humans, used to hunt food and then go off food for days. Our body has been evolved in a similar fashion. If you observe wild animals, they will hunt , savor the meat, and then go days without food. Intermittent fasting has been the way of life for the animals. (Picture source: Pixabay) According to Ayurveda (Indian traditional medicine system) , it is suggested to eat dinner well before sunset and then again breaking the fast a few hours after the sunrise, the next morning. This will take about 14–16 hours, and can be considered as Intermittent Fasting. Many religions like Hindus, Muslims etc have been observing fasting in various occasions since thousands of years. So, telling it a “present trend” will be wrong. So why Intermittent Fasting? (Picture source: Wall Street Journal) The main benefit of Intermittent Fasting is Autophagy. As you can see, Yoshinori Oshumi, a Japanese researcher, has been awarded Nobel Prize for his discoveries of mechanisms for autophagy induced by Fasting. I’m trying to explain it in a rather simple way. Our cells keeps on dying and regenerating but not necessarily we are able to excrete the dead cells. The cells are stored in our body. When we are always in a feeding mode, we are not able to digest and excrete the dead cells because our body is busy in breaking down the food that we have ingested (not necessarily absorbed). In a fasted state, there’s nothing to digest hence, the body digests off the dead cells. It is way too vague to explain this way but the basic is the same only. (Picture Source: Pixabay) Now, you go to the gym, you have flaccid body then you do workouts, your body becomes sore and then you’ll have defined and toned muscles. How do the toned muscles form? It is formed by breaking of “unworked” muscle fibres and constant regeneration process. Now where do the old muscles go? They are stored in our body only! And constant accumulation of it results your body becoming a garbage can. The best way to throw it away , you got it right - “Autophagy”. And the best part, Intermittent Fasting actually helps in building those muscles!! There are numerous other benefits of Intermittent Fasting , like increased Metabolism, increment in Growth Hormone secretion, better handling of stress, reduction in Kidney diseases, increased longevity so on and so forth. There are multiple researches done to back this claim. And weight loss, or I should say “Fat Loss” is just a “Side-effect”

For example; when someone hurts us, its sometimes better to teach them a lesson without any bitterness or anger rather with compassion, so that the person can learn a valuable lesson and can live a more fulfilled life. Disciples said that the gift would be with the person that was trying to gift us. “Exactly!” Buddha said. If you donot accept the abuse, the abuse will be with the abuser and not with us. Name: CA. Suyog Upadhyaya
Question: How do you stop beating yourself up when you made the big mistake of your life?
Answer: First of all, I’d like the seeker to know that they are on the right track if they are beating themselves up after making the big mistake of their life. Because, it means that they have realized their mistake which most people fail to do and end up in vicious cycles hurting others. The world runs on cause and effect. The mistake is the cause, the guilt is the effect. Yes, there are various external effects as well, but the most foundational ones are the sensations within. The effect comes up to give us learning, to break the cycle of karma (Cause/Work) and its “Fala” (Effect/Result). When we understand the the beating up that we are experiencing is the basic natural phenomenon then , we realize that we have to take it as an opportunity to learn and evolve. I’m no way an expert , because there are times where I make mistakes and I repent. Not always I am in a great unison with my senses. But here is a simple technique I use: Firstly, take 10–15 deep breaths, and then observe normal breath for about 5 minutes. Then observe the sensations from top of the head to tips of the toes. During the time many thoughts will come, do not try to avoid it, rather focus on sensations. Then recreate the whole scenario and try analyzing the situation from first person view (i.e., your own view). Analyse why you did what you did. What made you do such? What were the circumstances then, explore possible explanations. There will be many. Then, observe the scenario from second person perspective (For example if you had an argument, try watching the scenario from the view of person with whom you argued). Feel how the second person would have felt and why the did what they did. Finally, observe the scenario from a neutral perspective. Like you’re watching a movie but detached with the character. Analyse why it happened. Yes, it will not go in a single instance, there is no magic pill. Rather its like a workout. Take your time to realize that what had been done/said cannot be undone, and the best thing we can do is to mend the situation by making rational decisions formed after continuous exercise as mentioned above. You’ll certainly evolve as a better human being than you were before. Do not shy away from asking for forgiveness or giving forgiveness. Our human life is very short. I wish you a happy life. Regards, S
